D013-D009_h001.question: It's been close to five months now, this… gloom. It’s hard to even put one foot in front of the other most days. At the zoo, I just shuffle from the primate enclosure to the big cats, barely speaking. My wife notices the slowdown too; she says I’m moving like a sloth in slow motion. I find myself just bursting into tears for no reason, sometimes right there in front of the capybaras. Then the guilt cycles start – replaying every single mistake I’ve ever made, every animal I could’ve fed better, every cross word I’ve ever said to my wife. It’s like a broken record in my head. And sometimes, usually when I’m up high cleaning out an aviary, or driving to work, I get this terrifying urge to just… let go, or swerve into oncoming traffic. No plan, just this sudden, horrific impulse. It’s draining, utterly draining. Sometimes, maybe for a day or two, I’ll feel a burst of energy, almost too much, and I’ll get a bunch of projects done around the house really fast, but it never lasts. Then it’s back to this.
D013-D009_h001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h001.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h002.question:
Lately, I’ve just felt… off. It's been about five months now, and it’s really messing with my work. I can barely focus on coding; my employer has noticed. I find myself tearing up out of nowhere, even over small things. And I can't sit still – I'm constantly pacing around my apartment or picking at my cuticles, just a general restless feeling.

Everything feels like my fault, too. If a project at work hits a snag, even if it’s outside my control, I instantly blame myself and feel like I deserve whatever bad consequences might come. There's this thought that keeps popping into my head, not like I want to actively hurt myself, but more like a quiet "I wish I just wouldn't wake up tomorrow."

Sometimes, though, it’s like a switch flips. For a few days, I feel intensely focused and wired, pulling all-nighters coding, feeling like I’m on top of the world. My thoughts race, and I’m full of ideas. But it doesn't last, and then I crash back into this heavy emptiness, feeling even worse than before. Those 'up' periods are short, a few days at most. I haven’t really had anything that lasts longer.
D013-D009_h002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h002.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h003.question:

I feel so worthless, like my contributions at work or even at home with my husband just don’t matter. It’s not that I want to hurt myself, but sometimes I just wish I wouldn't wake up.

There have also been these weird bursts, you know? Like for a few days, I’ll have all this energy, feel incredibly productive, barely sleep. My husband has even commented that I’m talking a mile a minute. I’ll start a million projects, convinced they're brilliant ideas for work or around the house, only to crash a few days later back into this emptiness. It makes it so hard to get anything done consistently.
D013-D009_h003.options:

    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h017.question:

D013-D009_h021.question:

D013-D009_h022.question:

Then there are these… impulses. Sometimes, standing on a bridge, part of me just wants to jump. Or driving, there's this sudden urge to just swerve into oncoming traffic. No plan, not like I’d ever do it, but the thought just… flashes. It’s unnerving.

    D. Major Depressive Disorder

My ex-wife notices how distant I am, how I’m not myself. It’s hard to keep up appearances at work; I used to thrive on pressure, now it just feels like too much. There are brief periods, a few days here and there, when I feel a surge of energy, like I can conquer anything, but they never last. Then it’s back to this emptiness.
